context.situation: You're at Istanbul Airport on your way to a conference in London. The departures board says your flight is cancelled. You go to the airline desk.
context.situation_ar: أنت في مطار إسطنبول في طريقك إلى مؤتمر في لندن. لوحة المغادرة تقول إن رحلتك أُلغيت. تذهب إلى مكتب شركة الطيران.
context.goal: Explain a travel problem, understand your options and get what you need.
context.goal_ar: أن تشرح مشكلة سفر، وتفهم الخيارات المتاحة، وتحصل على ما تحتاجه.

script.t: Good afternoon. How can I help?
Hi. My flight to London has been cancelled, and I've got a conference tomorrow morning.
I'm sorry about that. Can I see your boarding pass?
Thank you. OK, I'm afraid the next direct flight is full. I can put you on the ten p.m. flight via Amsterdam, or on the first direct flight tomorrow at seven.
What time does the Amsterdam flight get in?
Just after one in the morning, local time.
Hmm. And my suitcase? I've already checked it in.
It'll be transferred automatically. So, have you made a decision yet?
I'll take the Amsterdam flight. I can't risk missing the first session.
No problem. Here's your new boarding pass, and a meal voucher for the wait.
That's great. Thanks for your help.

gist.prompt: What is the outcome of the conversation?
options: Yusuf gets a seat on an indirect flight tonight.
Yusuf decides to fly tomorrow morning.

detail.prompt: Why can't Yusuf get the next direct flight?
What will happen to his suitcase?
options: It will go to London automatically.
He must collect it in Amsterdam.

detail.text: So, have you ___ a decision yet?

inference.prompt: Why does Yusuf choose the Amsterdam flight?
options: The seven o'clock flight might not get him there in time.
The agent tells him he has to.

explain.1: He never says that. Listen to "I can't risk missing the first session."
explain.2: The agent offers two options — Yusuf chooses.

notice.quote: My flight has been cancelled. … I've already checked it in.

question.prompt: Why does Yusuf use the present perfect (has been / I've checked) and not a past time?
options: The past action matters NOW — it's the reason he's at the desk.
It happened a long time ago.
He doesn't know when it happened.

notice.explain: Present perfect: a past event with a result now. We don't say when. (Compare: The flight was cancelled at 2 p.m.)
notice.explain_ar: المضارع التام: حدث ماضٍ له نتيجة الآن، ولا نذكر متى حدث.

notice.quote: I'm afraid the next direct flight is full.

options: No — it's a polite way to give bad news.

notice.explain: "I'm afraid…" softens bad news. It's very common in service situations.

grammar.title: Present perfect for news and results
grammar.context: My flight has been cancelled. I've already checked my suitcase in.
grammar.pattern: have / has + past participle  (passive: has been + past participle)
examples: Have you made a decision yet?
grammar.explain: Use it for recent events that matter now, without a finished time. With a finished time (yesterday, at 2 p.m.) use the past simple.
grammar.explain_ar: للأحداث القريبة المهمة الآن دون ذكر وقت منتهٍ.

practice.text: Excuse me, I think I ___ (lose) my boarding pass.

errors.why: It's news with a result now (you don't have it), so use have + lost.
errors.why_ar: استخدم have lost لأن النتيجة الآن.

practice.text: Our flight ___ (land) at 6 a.m. this morning.

errors.why: "At 6 a.m. this morning" is a finished time, so use the past simple.

answers: Have you made a decision yet?

pairs: the document you show at the gate
give your suitcase to the airline
a polite way to give bad news

answers: My luggage has not arrived yet.
practice.why: With yet (up to now) we use the present perfect.

pronunciation.title: /p/ or /b/?
pronunciation.tip: Arabic has no /p/. For /p/ push a small puff of air out — hold paper in front of your mouth: it should move.
pronunciation.tip_ar: لا يوجد صوت /p/ في العربية. عند نطقه أخرج دفعة هواء صغيرة.

pronunciation.title: Contractions
pronunciation.tip: Have/has become very short: I've, it's, she's.

pronunciation.title: Shadowing
pronunciation.tip: Stay calm and polite — your tone matters as much as your words.
